samplingMethod: Read-only checkout C:\src\lft-air at HEAD 8731a8b. Pools are built in file order. (1) exercises: every exercise of every lesson of every unit of every section in content/courses/es-vi.json (N=718). (2) stories: every sentence in content/es/stories/stories.json with a non-empty translation.vi, story by story, id '<storyId>#s<index>' (N=463). (3) reception: every block of every reading in content/es/reception/reading.json ('<readingId>#b<i>'), then every segment of every clip in listening.json ('<clipId>#g<i>'), then every node of every scenario in interaction/scenarios.json in object-key order ('<scenarioId>#<nodeId>'), including partner, learner and terminal nodes (N=597: 82 reading + 265 listening + 250 scenario). (4) applied fixes: entries in content/es/_drafts/review/decisions-pass2.json and then decisions-audit.json whose decision string starts with 'fixed', in key order (N=77). A single rng = random.Random(20261030) then draws, in this order: rng.sample(range(N1), round(0.10*N1)), rng.sample(range(N2), round(0.10*N2)), rng.sample(range(N3), round(0.10*N3)), rng.sample(range(N4), 10). Indices are sorted. Sizes drawn: 72 exercises + 46 story sentences + 60 reception units (10 % of 597, more than the briefed ~50) = 178. All lines are eligible, whether or not they changed. Context (whole story, whole scenario, linked clip or reading) was read wherever needed. Grading was judged against src/lib/grading.ts, src/lib/speech/grader.ts (whole-utterance variants OR contiguous concept runs) and src/lib/languages/es.ts. Scripts: scratchpad review/pools.py (sampling), dump.py, look.py, story.py, fixes.py, verify_fixes.py.

findings.reason: The lexicon glosses es:w:mama as "mẹ / má". The course does not teach mamá before this exercise, so few learners will produce it, but it is a correct answer for "Mẹ tôi".

findings.reason: Accent folding already accepts "Hanoi". A Vietnamese learner who writes the city in its Vietnamese form gives two tokens ("ha noi") and is marked wrong. That is a proper-noun spelling, not a Spanish error.

findings.current: distractor "xin chào" for prompt "buenos días" (key "chào buổi sáng")
findings.proposed: replace the distractor with "chào buổi tối" (or "chúc ngủ ngon")
findings.reason: In everyday Vietnamese "xin chào" is how one renders a "buenos días" greeting, so the distractor can be defended. The key is still the best option, so learners are not wrongly marked, but the option set is weaker than it should be.
